paras: The lynching of George Washington was the hanging of a Black man by a mob in Tennessee, reported in early August 1880. According to a Kentucky paper, Washington was taken from the jail at Denver, Tennessee, and lynched for the murder of Egbert Fagan. The case reached readers mainly as a one-line item in crime roundups printed in the Midwest.

Washington, described as "colored," was held in the jail at Denver, Tennessee, on an accusation of murdering a man named Egbert Fagan. He was taken from the jail and hanged by a mob. None of the reports gives the date, saying only that he was hanged "recently" in items printed from 5 August 1880. The size and makeup of the mob, the jailer's actions, and the circumstances of Fagan's death are not described.
No report of an inquest, arrests or other official response appears in the coverage.

The first notices appeared on 5 August 1880 in a wire column titled "Recent Tragedies," which called Washington "a colored murderer" who "was recently hanged by a mob, in the backwoods of Tennessee." The same wording ran that day in the Topeka Tribune under the heading "HANGED BY A MOB." and two days later in the Superior Times in Wisconsin. The Mankato Free Press printed a reworded version, saying he "was hung by a mob in the backwoods of Tennessee recently." In each case the item sat among dozens of other crimes, with no comment on the mob.

Only the South Kentuckian of Hopkinsville, published on 10 August, named the town, the jail and the alleged victim, in a single unadorned sentence. Neither it nor the Topeka Tribune, which ran the wire wording unchanged, added any comment of its own. No account from a Tennessee paper appears in the coverage.

reader.title: Lynching of George Washington (Denver, Tennessee)
bases: All reports say a mob hanged or lynched George Washington, a Black man accused of murder, and one says he was taken from the jail at Denver, Tennessee (A1, A3, A5).

He was hanged by a 'mob' (A1, A2, A3) after being taken from jail (A5), with no lawful authority, as punishment for an alleged murder (A5); the mob's size is not given, but the word 'mob' and the jail seizure indicate a group.
A widely reprinted wire item (A1, A2, A3) and a differently worded, more detailed Kentucky report (A5) agree that a mob killed George Washington, a Black man accused of murder, in Tennessee.

accounts.gist: Geo. Washington, colored, was taken from the jail at Denver, Tenn., and lynched for the murder of Egbert Fagan.

framing.detail: Minnesota and Wisconsin papers ran the item in 'Recent Tragedies' columns, calling Washington 'a colored murderer' with no comment on the mob.
The South Kentuckian gave a bare one-sentence notice naming the jail, town and alleged victim, with no comment.
The Topeka Tribune ran the wire wording under the heading 'HANGED BY A MOB.' without comment.

versions.value: taken from the jail at Denver, Tenn.

conflicts.note: Not contradictory: the wire item is vague, and the South Kentuckian, published closer to the scene, is more specific.

record_check.dossier: No report gives a date; the earliest report is 1880-08-05 and says 'recently'. Late July is plausible but not stated.
No article read names the county; only 'Denver Tenn.' is given.
Four reports of the episode and one identical reprint, 1880-08-05 to 1880-08-10; no Black-press or Tennessee coverage found.
